title: BLA 761269/S-001 GENERAL ADVICE CORRECTION OF POSTMARKETING REQUIREMENT (PMR) AND POSTMARKETING COMMITMENT (PMC) SET/NUMBERS

themes: ARIA risk in ApoE ε4 homozygotes
one_line: The FDA confirms Leqembi's clinical benefit while mandating extensive postmarketing studies to monitor severe ARIA and intracerebral hemorrhage risks, particularly in ApoE ε4 homozygotes.
summary: This document contains an FDA supplement approval letter for Leqembi (lecanemab-irmb) and a subsequent general advice letter correcting the tracking numbers for its postmarketing requirements. The approval letter confirms that Study 301 verified the drug's clinical benefit, officially granting it traditional approval. Crucially, the FDA outlines new safety information revealing an increased risk of severe amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA) in ApoE ε4 homozygotes and intracerebral hemorrhages in patients with preexisting risk factors. To address these concerns, the FDA mandates a comprehensive set of postmarketing requirements (PMRs) and commitments (PMCs). Eisai must conduct a prospective observational registry study and execute a retrospective cohort study using claims data to track real-world clinical safety outcomes. The FDA also mandates a randomized clinical trial featuring ApoE ε4 homozygotes to further characterize safety profiles in this vulnerable population. Furthermore, the agency requires the analytical validation of an in vitro diagnostic device to accurately identify ApoE ε4 alleles prior to treatment. Finally, strict biannual pharmacovigilance reporting is mandated to continuously monitor ARIA events, intracerebral hemorrhages, and infusion reactions.

key_claims.claim: Leqembi increases the risk of symptomatic, serious, and severe radiographic ARIA in ApoE ε4 homozygotes compared to heterozygotes and noncarriers.
key_claims.evidence: FDA citation of new clinical trial data indicating increased ARIA risk specific to ApoE ε4 homozygotes.

key_claims.claim: Leqembi increases the risk of intracerebral hemorrhage >1 cm in patients with risk factors such as cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA) and anticoagulant use.
key_claims.evidence: FDA citation of new clinical trial data showing intracerebral hemorrhage >1 cm in patients taking Leqembi who have preexisting bleeding risk factors.

key_claims.claim: Study BAN2401-G000-301 successfully verified the clinical benefit of Leqembi.
key_claims.evidence: FDA review and approval of the final clinical study report for Study 301, fulfilling PMR 4384-1.

methods.population: Alzheimer's disease patients treated with lecanemab-irmb

limitations: The document asserts new safety information based on clinical trial data but does not provide the primary data, event rates, or statistical analyses within the text itself.

issues: Page numbers and headers are interspersed throughout the text.
